zotero.abstractNote: Structural brain alterations associated with depression and anxiety are subtle, heterogeneous, and difficult to characterize. We applied autoencoder-based normative modeling to T1-weighted MRI data from the UK Biobank (N=38,454) to map individual-level deviations in brain structure. We identified a shared pattern of structural deviations associated with both depression and anxiety, which was robustly replicated in an independent cohort (N=1,154). These deviations were linked to specific genetic and environmental factors, suggesting a common biological substrate for these disorders. Our findings demonstrate that structural brain deviations reflect meaningful, continuous variation in affective and behavioral symptoms.
